scores.reason: The pay slot opens correctly, but the primary_text is built almost entirely of filler: 'exciting opportunity,' 'dynamic team,' 'competitive pay,' 'family atmosphere,' 'truly value our drivers,' 'take your career to the next level.' No route, no schedule detail beyond the pay figure, no company name. Spanish mirrors the same filler word-for-word.

This candidate advertises flatbed and home weekends — neither is a fact in the brief, which calls for reefer, regional, and home weekly. The pay figure ($450/load) also does not appear in the facts. While the Spanish is natural and the copy is clean, it describes a completely different job.

Opens with the higher pay figure as the hook, then delivers every checkable fact: route (Chicago to Texas), freight type (reefer, no-touch), schedule (home weekly, weekly pay), pay range ($0.62–$0.70/mile), requirements (23+, 2 years), and company name. Spanish is natural, uses 'tráiler refrigerado,' 'rutas,' 'carga,' and keeps miles in miles — closest to how a dispatcher would actually talk.
